sources.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources.locator: {{rd|melee|ranged}} template convention, cross-checked across the cache
sources.quote: Ravenous Hydra / Profane Hydra Cleave '{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}'; Blade of the Ruined King '{{rd|9%|6%}}'; Death's Dance '{{rd|30%|10%}}'
sources.conclusion: First argument = melee holder, second = ranged holder. Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is therefore 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder).

sources.quote: Carve: 'Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.'  Fervor: 'Dealing {{as|physical damage}} grants you {{as|20 '''bonus''' movement speed}} for 2 seconds.'
sources.conclusion: Black Cleaver carries NO damage amplifier. Its only combat effect is armor reduction, which acts on the target's resistance R and can therefore only move a post-mitigation `damage` leaf, never a pre-mitigation `raw_damage` leaf. Stats: 40 AD / 400 HP / 20 AH (no amp).

sources.quote: the mitigation operator `x -> x*100/(100+R)` is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance
sources.conclusion: A damage amplifier commutes with mitigation, so folding an 'increased damage taken' multiplier into the ledger's `raw_damage` is numerically equivalent to applying it after mitigation. The engine's own diff (a raw leaf moving on an amp-only scenario) shows this is the convention in use.

sources.locator: Section 2.1 / 2.2 / Section 5 audit table (resistance, penetration, reduction)
sources.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)  (apply_resistance, resistance.py); reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R <- R - r_flat; R <- R*(1 - r_pct/100)
sources.conclusion: All Black Cleaver machinery lives on the R axis. Confirms the only mechanism in this scenario that can move a raw value is Bloodsong's Expose Weakness.

sources.quote: grant you 8% increased damage against champions until 5 seconds after exiting combat with them  /  "damage_amp_ratio": 0.08
sources.conclusion: The only OTHER 8% amplifier in the whole cache. It is attacker-side and belongs to a keystone, not to either item this scenario is named for. Listed here because it is the one thing that could legitimise a second 8% factor - and it is not part of the scenario's named loadout.

sources.file: data/items.json (survey of every 'increased damage' string in the cache)
sources.quote: Amplifier inventory: Bloodsong 8%/5% (target debuff), Riftmaker 2%/s to 8%, Spear of Shojin 3%/stack to 12%, Haunting Guise & Liandry's 2%/s to 6%, Immortal Path 4%, Prowler's Claw 20%, Shadowflame 20%, Hexoptics 10%, Lord Dominik's/Perplexity up to 15%, Diamond-Tipped 30%/50%
sources.conclusion: No item in the scenario's name other than Bloodsong supplies any amplifier, and no combination of the two named items yields a 16.6% multiplier.

computation.step_2_identify_factor: 1.08^2 = 1.1664 and 94.1 x 1.1664 = 109.7582 -> 109.8 at the golden file's 1-decimal rounding. The change is therefore exactly TWO multiplicative applications of the melee 8% Expose Weakness amplifier. Checks that fail: single 8% -> 101.6; single 5% -> 98.8; double 5% (1.05^2) -> 103.7; additive 8%+8% (1.16) -> 109.2; additive 8%+5% (1.13) -> 106.3. Only 1.08 x 1.08 reproduces 109.8.
computation.step_3_amp_count_in_old: Since new/old = 1.08^2 exactly, the new value carries exactly two more 8% factors than the old. 'old = one application, new = two' would have produced 94.1 x 1.08 = 101.6, not 109.8. So the old value carries ZERO amplifier factors: 94.1 is the unamplified pre-mitigation raw.
computation.step_4_legitimate_amp_count: Expose Weakness is a single named debuff on the target ('inflict them with Expose Weakness for 4 seconds, causing them to take 8% increased damage from all sources'), carried by a passive flagged "unique": true, with a 1.5 s reapplication cooldown. It is one debuff on one target: additional Bloodsong holders refresh it rather than stack it, and a team may field only one support item in any case. Black Cleaver contributes no amplifier (S3). Legitimate factor count for this scenario = 1.
computation.step_6_verdict: 94.1 omits the amplifier entirely (understates by 8%); 109.8 applies it twice (overstates by 8% over the correct 101.6). Neither is the sourced value.

residual_uncertainty: Scenario definitions are not in data/ (the golden corpus lives under scripts/, which this runbook forbids), so the roster composition is inferred from the scenario name plus the cached item text. The named loadout is Black Cleaver + Bloodsong.

If the scenario's Bloodsong holder is RANGED, the sourced amplifier is 5% and the correct value would be 94.1 x 1.05 = 98.8 - still neither the old nor the new value. The fact that the observed factor is exactly 1.08^2 (and not 1.05^2 = 103.7) shows the engine used the melee 8% branch.

109.8 would be correct only if a SECOND, independent 8% amplifier were active on this event - the only candidate in the cache is the Press the Attack keystone's damage_amp_ratio 0.08 (S6), which neither named item supplies. If the scenario does carry that keystone, the verdict would flip to new_value_correct; nothing in the data tree indicates it does.

If the engine's ledger convention were instead to keep amplifiers out of raw_damage entirely (applying them to the post-mitigation `damage` field, as the game does), the old 94.1 would be correct. The diff itself - a raw leaf moving on a scenario whose only damage-affecting new mechanism is an amplifier - establishes that the convention in force folds the amp into raw, which is numerically legitimate by the linearity quoted in S4.

verdict_detail.new_error: +8.2 (109.8 vs 101.6): amplifier applied twice (1.08^2 instead of 1.08)
